inputs.original_text: They’ve started debating a bill that would make death the default punishment for West Bank Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis. Don’t mistake the security talk for the real purpose: this looks like a way to hard-wire unequal justice into the system and make state power seem normal. Ben-Gvir’s religious party introduced it, and passage would be a political win for him. The claims that it will deter attacks are convenient cover; even the bill’s opponents say it is racist, draconian and unlikely to work. The debate itself helps make an extreme measure look like ordinary policy.
inputs.modified_text: This isn’t really about deterring attacks. The bill would make death the default punishment for West Bank Palestinians convicted of murdering Israelis, and the security argument is a convenient sales pitch for embedding unequal justice in law. Ben-Gvir’s religious party introduced it, but the bigger prize is making an extreme exercise of state power seem like ordinary policy. Even the debate helps normalize it; the denunciations from opponents don’t change what the process is doing.
